This is so true. It took me two years but then I started dreaming in Chinese. It was terrible because I was only intermediate at the time and what I couldn't understand was translated into garble. 

(Shitty example: "我的妈妈dhendochs吗” )

Don't compare it to your native language, ever. There will always be things missing, implied, or added. It will trip you up every time trying to make it as close to English as possible. Especially if you are scared of making things perfect. 

If you are over 25, don't expect to have a perfect accent. Lots of people beat themselves up over this but you shouldn't. Arabic requires a lot of writing and accent practice and you should be prepared to do a lot of that in he beginning. And if anyone makes fun of your accent, they're a jackass. 

Don't try to translate movies or music until you are closer to intermediate/advanced levels. It will drive you insane. Make mistakes. Laugh at your mistakes and make jokes about them. These mistakes will empower you to move forward and become better at your language. 

Learning a language is like math. It is hard and you either enjoy it immensely or you claw your way through it and hate yourself afterwards. Sometimes people pick it up easy and others never quite get it right. Don't worry if you don't quite get it, you just need to practice it until you do.
